title: Genesis Chapter 39 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 39 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 39 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 39.

questions.question: Who bought Joseph when he was brought down to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Potiphar
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:1 states that Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, bought Joseph from the Ishmeelites.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD was with Joseph and he was prosperous while in Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:2 says the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man in his master's house.

questions.question: What did Joseph's master observe about him?
options: The LORD was with Joseph and made all he did prosper
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was with Joseph and made all he did prosper
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:3 explains that Joseph's master saw the LORD was with him and prospered all he did.

questions.question: What position did Joseph's master give him in his house?
questions.correctAnswer: Overseer over his house
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:4 states Joseph was made overseer over his master's house and all he had.

questions.question: For whose sake did the LORD bless the Egyptian's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph's
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:5 says the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake.

questions.question: What did Potiphar know about what he owned after putting Joseph in charge?
options: He knew everything about his possessions
He only knew about the bread he ate
He knew about the fields but not the house
He knew about the house but not the fields
questions.correctAnswer: He only knew about the bread he ate
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:6 states Potiphar knew not anything he had except the bread he ate, leaving all in Joseph's hand.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph was described as a goodly person and well favoured.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:6 describes Joseph as a goodly person and well favoured.

questions.question: What did Potiphar's wife ask Joseph to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Lie with her
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:7 records that Potiphar's wife cast her eyes on Joseph and said, 'Lie with me.'

questions.question: How did Joseph respond to Potiphar's wife's request?
options: He refused and explained his loyalty to his master and God
questions.correctAnswer: He refused and explained his loyalty to his master and God
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:8-9 show Joseph refused, saying it would be a great wickedness and sin against God.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph said there was none greater in the house than himself except Potiphar's wife.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:9 states Joseph said there was none greater in the house than himself, nor had his master kept anything from him except his wife.

questions.question: What did Joseph do when Potiphar's wife caught him by his garment?
options: He stayed and talked with her
He left his garment in her hand and fled
questions.correctAnswer: He left his garment in her hand and fled
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:12 tells how Joseph left his garment in her hand and fled when she caught him.

questions.question: What false accusation did Potiphar's wife make against Joseph?
options: He tried to mock her and lie with her
questions.correctAnswer: He tried to mock her and lie with her
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:14-15 show she accused Joseph of bringing an Hebrew to mock her and lie with her.

questions.question: What was the consequence for Joseph after Potiphar heard his wife's words?
options: He was put into the prison
He was sent back to his family
questions.correctAnswer: He was put into the prison
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:20 states Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison.

questions.question: True or False: Even while in prison, the LORD was with Joseph and gave him favor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:21 confirms the LORD was with Joseph in prison, showing him mercy and giving him favor.

questions.question: Who did Joseph have authority over while in prison?
questions.correctAnswer: All the prisoners
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:22 says the keeper of the prison put all the prisoners into Joseph's hand.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 39 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 39 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How did Joseph's master, Potiphar, respond to Joseph's faithful service in his house?
options: He made Joseph overseer over his house and everything he had
He sent Joseph back to his family
questions.correctAnswer: He made Joseph overseer over his house and everything he had
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:4 states that Joseph found grace in his master's sight, who then made him overseer over his house and all that he had. This shows Potiphar's trust in Joseph's faithfulness and competence.

questions.question: What reason does Joseph give for refusing to lie with Potiphar's wife?
options: He fears his master would punish him
He does not want to sin against God
He is afraid of the men of the house
questions.correctAnswer: He does not want to sin against God
questions.explanation: In Genesis 39:9, Joseph explains that committing this act would be a great wickedness and a sin against God, demonstrating his integrity and faithfulness to God's commandments.

questions.question: What does Genesis 39:10 reveal about Joseph's response to Potiphar's wife's repeated advances?
options: He gave in to her request
questions.correctAnswer: He hearkened not unto her
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that Joseph did not listen to her or yield to her attempts, demonstrating his steadfast obedience and self-control (Genesis 39:10).

questions.question: Why was Joseph alone in the house when Potiphar's wife tried to seduce him?
options: He went into the house to do his business and no men were there
He was locked in the house intentionally
The men were outside working in the field
questions.correctAnswer: He went into the house to do his business and no men were there
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:11 explains that Joseph went into the house to do his business, and at that time, none of the men of the house were there, setting the scene for the incident.

questions.question: What did Joseph leave in Potiphar's wife's hand when he fled?
questions.correctAnswer: His garment
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:12 states that as Joseph fled, he left his garment in her hand, which later became evidence in the false accusation against him.

questions.question: What false accusation did Potiphar's wife make against Joseph?
options: That Joseph tried to mock and lie with her
That Joseph stole from the house
That Joseph ran away from his duties
questions.correctAnswer: That Joseph tried to mock and lie with her
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:14 records her telling the men of her house that Joseph, an Hebrew, came to mock her and tried to lie with her, which was untrue and motivated by her own actions.

questions.question: How does this passage teach about integrity and faithfulness under temptation?
options: Joseph refuses to sin against God despite repeated temptation
Joseph gives in to temptation but repents later
Joseph avoids the situation by running away immediately
Joseph reports the temptation to his master
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph refuses to sin against God despite repeated temptation
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:8-10 show Joseph's refusal to lie with his master's wife, citing his desire not to sin against God, illustrating integrity and faithfulness even under pressure.

questions.question: What was the immediate consequence for Joseph after Potiphar's wife made her accusation?
options: He was put into the king's prison
He was sent back to his family
He was promoted to a higher position
questions.correctAnswer: He was put into the king's prison
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:20 states that Joseph's master took him and put him into prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound, as a result of the false accusation.

questions.question: What does Genesis 39:21-23 reveal about God's presence with Joseph in prison?
options: The LORD showed him mercy and gave him favor with the keeper
Joseph was forgotten and left alone
Joseph lost all blessings and favor
The keeper was harsh and unkind to Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD showed him mercy and gave him favor with the keeper
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize God's mercy and favor toward Joseph even in prison, enabling him to prosper and be trusted with responsibility (Genesis 39:21-23).

questions.question: How does Genesis 39 demonstrate the importance of trusting God during trials?
options: Joseph remains faithful and prospers despite false accusations
Joseph abandons his faith under pressure
God immediately frees Joseph from prison
Joseph seeks revenge against his accuser
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph remains faithful and prospers despite false accusations
questions.explanation: Throughout Genesis 39, Joseph trusts the LORD, who is with him and causes him to prosper even in adverse circumstances such as imprisonment (Genesis 39:2, 21-23).

questions.question: What does Genesis 39:16 show about Potiphar's wife's actions after the incident with Joseph?
options: She laid up Joseph's garment until her husband came home
She gave the garment back to Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: She laid up Joseph's garment until her husband came home
questions.explanation: Verse 16 explains that she kept Joseph’s garment to use as evidence when her husband returned, showing premeditation in her false accusation (Genesis 39:16).

questions.question: Based on Genesis 39:8-9, what biblical virtue does Joseph demonstrate by refusing Potiphar's wife's offer?
options: Integrity and fear of sinning against God
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity and fear of sinning against God
questions.explanation: Joseph's refusal is grounded in his integrity and the fear of sinning against God, as stated in Genesis 39:9, showing his commitment to righteous living.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph was the only person who knew about the temptation from Potiphar's wife.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text shows that only Joseph and Potiphar's wife were involved in the temptation; the men of the house were not present (Genesis 39:11-12).

questions.question: True or False: Potiphar's wife admitted that Joseph did not try to lie with her but she misunderstood his actions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Potiphar's wife falsely accused Joseph of trying to mock and lie with her, deliberately lying to her husband (Genesis 39:14-15).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's blessing on Joseph's work extended even to the prison where he was confined.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:21-23 shows that the LORD was with Joseph in prison, granting him favor and making all he did prosper, even there.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 39 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 39.

questions.question: What accusation did Potiphar's wife make against Joseph?
options: That he tried to mock her
That he stole from the house
That he was plotting against Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: That he tried to mock her
questions.explanation: Potiphar's wife accused Joseph of coming into her to mock her, as stated in Genesis 39:17.

questions.question: What did Joseph leave behind when he fled from Potiphar's wife?
questions.correctAnswer: His garment
questions.explanation: Joseph left his garment in her hand when he fled, demonstrating his refusal to sin, according to Genesis 39:18.

questions.question: How did Potiphar react upon hearing his wife's accusation against Joseph?
options: He believed Joseph and released him
questions.correctAnswer: His wrath was kindled
questions.explanation: Potiphar's anger was kindled when he heard his wife's words accusing Joseph, as stated in Genesis 39:19.

questions.question: Where was Joseph imprisoned after Potiphar believed his wife's accusation?
options: In a place where the king's prisoners were bound
questions.correctAnswer: In a place where the king's prisoners were bound
questions.explanation: Joseph was put into the prison where the king's prisoners were bound, according to Genesis 39:20.

questions.question: What was the LORD's relationship to Joseph while he was in prison?
options: The LORD was with Joseph and showed him mercy
The LORD sent an angel to free Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was with Joseph and showed him mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:21 states that the LORD was with Joseph, showed him mercy, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

questions.question: What responsibility was given to Joseph in prison?
options: To oversee all the prisoners and their activities
questions.correctAnswer: To oversee all the prisoners and their activities
questions.explanation: Joseph was put in charge of all the prisoners and whatever was done there, as described in Genesis 39:22.

questions.question: Why did the keeper of the prison not worry about anything under his charge during Joseph's administration?
options: Because Joseph was a fierce enforcer
Because the LORD was with Joseph and made his work prosper
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD was with Joseph and made his work prosper
questions.explanation: The keeper did not worry because the LORD was with Joseph and caused his work to prosper, according to Genesis 39:23.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'mock' used in Genesis 39:17 can also mean which of the following?
options: To make sport of or scorn
questions.correctAnswer: To make sport of or scorn
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word used for 'mock' (לָעַג, la'ag) means to scorn or make sport of, which fits the accusation Potiphar's wife made against Joseph in Genesis 39:17.

questions.question: How does the theme of God's favor shown to Joseph in prison (Genesis 39:21-23) foreshadow later events in his life?
options: It foreshadows his rise to power in Egypt
It foreshadows his return to Canaan
It foreshadows his punishment by Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows his rise to power in Egypt
questions.explanation: The LORD's favor shown to Joseph in prison prefigures his eventual rise to a position of great authority in Egypt, as later detailed in Genesis 41.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Joseph's righteous refusal to sin against God despite temptation?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 10:13
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 10:13 speaks of God providing a way to escape temptation, reflecting Joseph’s refusal to sin against God as seen in Genesis 39:9.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Genesis 39 to contrast Joseph's integrity with the false accusation by Potiphar's wife?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: The chapter uses irony by showing Joseph’s innocence and integrity contrasted with the false accusation, emphasizing injustice (Genesis 39:7-20).

questions.question: Based on Genesis 39:19-20, what was the consequence of Potiphar's wife's false accusation for Joseph?
options: He was sent back to Canaan
He was promoted to a higher position
He was sold to another master
questions.correctAnswer: He was imprisoned
questions.explanation: Potiphar's belief of his wife's false accusation led to Joseph being imprisoned, as stated in Genesis 39:20.

questions.question: In the cultural context of ancient Egypt, what was significant about Potiphar making Joseph overseer of his entire house (Genesis 39:4-5)?
options: It indicated complete trust and authority over his assets
It was a ceremonial role with no real power
It was a punishment for Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: It indicated complete trust and authority over his assets
questions.explanation: Being made overseer meant Joseph had full responsibility and trust, unusual for a foreign servant, showing his exceptional standing (Genesis 39:4-5).

questions.question: True or False: Joseph's refusal to lie with Potiphar's wife was motivated solely by fear of his master.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joseph refused not only because of his master but also because he would be sinning against God, as he says in Genesis 39:9.

questions.question: True or False: The keeper of the prison entrusted Joseph with authority over other prisoners because the LORD was with him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:21-22 explains that the LORD's presence with Joseph caused the keeper to place all prisoners under Joseph's charge.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 39 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 39 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by the LORD's presence with Joseph, causing him to prosper in the house of his Egyptian master?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:2 states that the LORD was with Joseph and made him prosperous, showing God's providential care over Joseph's life.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human temptation and moral integrity is taught by Joseph's refusal of his master's wife's advances?
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and resisting sin
questions.explanation: In Genesis 39:8-9, Joseph refuses to sin against God, demonstrating personal holiness and sanctification by resisting temptation.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Joseph's false accusation and imprisonment contribute to the broader redemptive history in Scripture?
options: It shows God's judgment on sin
It prefigures Christ's innocent suffering and vindication
It explains the origin of Egyptian slavery
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ's innocent suffering and vindication
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:19-20 recount Joseph's unjust imprisonment, a typology of Christ's innocent suffering (cf. Isaiah 53:7), contributing to the redemptive narrative.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by His showing mercy and granting favor to Joseph even while he was in prison?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:21 explicitly states that the LORD showed mercy to Joseph and gave him favor, highlighting God's merciful nature.

questions.question: What doctrine can be drawn from the fact that Joseph was made overseer over all of Potiphar's house and possessions despite being a foreign slave?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine sovereignty over human affairs
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:4 shows that God sovereignly elevated Joseph, demonstrating His control over worldly power and status.

questions.question: According to Genesis 39:6, how is Joseph described physically and what might this imply about his role in the narrative?
options: A goodly person and well favored
questions.correctAnswer: A goodly person and well favored
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:6 describes Joseph as a goodly person and well favored, implying he was attractive and thus a believable target of temptation and favor.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Genesis 39:5 and Genesis 39:23 regarding God's blessing on human labor even in adverse circumstances?
options: God's blessing depends on human merit
God's blessing can prosper even in prison as Joseph's example shows
questions.correctAnswer: God's blessing can prosper even in prison as Joseph's example shows
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:5 and 39:23 together show that God's blessing was upon Joseph's master's house and upon Joseph's work in prison, teaching God's sovereignty and blessing transcends circumstances.

questions.question: What does Joseph's statement in Genesis 39:9 reveal about his understanding of sin and accountability before God?
options: He recognizes sin as rebellion against God
He believes sin is only a social offense
questions.correctAnswer: He recognizes sin as rebellion against God
questions.explanation: Joseph says sinning against his master's wife would be 'great wickedness, and sin against God' (Genesis 39:9), indicating his awareness of divine accountability.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Genesis 39:12 and Genesis 39:20 provide about human suffering and divine purpose?
options: Suffering is always punishment for sin
God abandons the faithful in trials
Innocent suffering can lead to divine advancement and purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Innocent suffering can lead to divine advancement and purpose
questions.explanation: Joseph fled temptation (Genesis 39:12) but was falsely imprisoned (Genesis 39:20), illustrating innocent suffering that ultimately fits into God's sovereign plan.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the account in Genesis 39 shows God endorsing injustice by allowing Joseph to be imprisoned unfairly. What does Genesis 39:21-23 actually teach about God's involvement in such circumstances?
options: God is indifferent to human injustice
God shows mercy and causes Joseph's work to prosper even in prison
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy and causes Joseph's work to prosper even in prison
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:21-23 teaches that although Joseph suffered injustice, the LORD was with him, showed mercy, and ensured his prospering, highlighting God's sustaining grace amid trials.

questions.question: How does Genesis 39:10 demonstrate Joseph's perseverance in holiness despite persistent temptation?
options: He complains to others about temptation
questions.correctAnswer: He ignores the temptation daily
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:10 records Joseph's daily refusal to listen to his master's wife's advances, showing steadfastness in resisting sin.

questions.question: What theological lesson concerning God's faithfulness can be deduced from Joseph being entrusted with all prisoners while in prison, as stated in Genesis 39:22?
options: God's faithfulness leads to responsibility even in hardship
Only the free can serve God
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness leads to responsibility even in hardship
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:22 shows Joseph was given charge over all prisoners, reflecting God's faithfulness in entrusting His servants with responsibility regardless of external conditions.

questions.question: What do Genesis 39:14-15 teach about human sinfulness and false accusation?
options: False accusations are rare and insignificant
False accusations are a manifestation of human sinfulness and can cause unjust suffering
questions.correctAnswer: False accusations are a manifestation of human sinfulness and can cause unjust suffering
questions.explanation: In Genesis 39:14-15, Potiphar's wife falsely accuses Joseph, showing human sinfulness involved in deceit and slander causing innocent suffering.

questions.question: Combining Genesis 39:1 and 39:4, what theological insight emerges about God's providence working through human history and circumstances?
options: God's providence is limited to Israel
God uses even foreign rulers and slavery to accomplish His purposes
God's plan is thwarted by human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God uses even foreign rulers and slavery to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:1 shows Joseph sold into Egypt, and 39:4 that he was made overseer, teaching God's providence in using adverse circumstances and foreign powers for His redemptive plan.

questions.question: What does Genesis 39:17-18 reveal about the power of testimony and the effects of slander in a fallen world?
options: Slanderous testimony can provoke wrath and injustice
Only the guilty suffer from accusations
questions.correctAnswer: Slanderous testimony can provoke wrath and injustice
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:17-18 shows Potiphar's wife's false testimony causing her husband's wrath and Joseph's imprisonment, illustrating the destructive power of slander.
